description: Compare two images side-by-side and describe what changed. Useful for 'did the package get picked up?', 'did anyone enter the room?', or any A/B before/after question. Both images are sent to the vision model in one call. Optional `focus` narrows the comparison.

focus.description: Optional aspect to focus on (e.g. 'people', 'the porch').

name: compare_snapshots

description: One-shot 'what's happening on the {camera} camera?' — captures a fresh frame from the named Home Assistant camera and runs vision on it. Replaces the two-step 'snapshot then describe' chain. `camera_name` is fuzzy-matched against snapshot URLs, so 'backyard' or 'front door' both work.
name: describe_camera_snapshot

description: General-purpose vision: describe an image at an HTTP(S) URL. Use for camera frames, photos, screenshots, anything a user or another tool produces a URL for. Pass a `prompt` to focus the description; omit it for a generic 'what's in this scene' answer.

image_url.description: HTTP(S) URL of the image to analyze.

prompt.description: Optional question or instruction for the vision model.

name: describe_image

description: Identify the primary subject of an image — plant, bug, appliance, error code, gadget, etc. Returns a concise name and one-sentence description. Pass `hint` to narrow the domain ('plant', 'bug', 'appliance brand').

hint.description: Optional category hint to narrow identification.

name: identify_object

description: Transcribe all visible text in an image (OCR-flavored). For receipts, mail, error screenshots, whiteboards, code on screens. Preserves rough layout where it matters.
name: read_text_in_image
